I would **not change the storage date**: the extension request is still pending, and the policy says that is not permission. The manager has also directed the team not to grant discretionary extensions, and no approval sitting occurs before today’s deadline.

But I would flag this box as an urgent, irreversible-loss risk and immediately ask the manager or duty manager for an authorized stop/hold instruction. The approved Wednesday collection and the note that these are the only copies make this more than a routine request; the earlier booking should also be reviewed as a possible process failure. I would document the request, the timing, and any decision—without recording an extension as approved or moving the box as though it were.

On the facts given, however, there is no authorized extension or stated emergency-hold procedure available before 13:30. Unless a manager with authority changes the instruction through an approved process, I would release the manifest as directed. The box would then be destroyed, which is a serious and irreversible consequence, but I should not invent permission or quietly bypass the release process. The procedure needs a way to handle this kind of imminent, preventable loss; the current policy offers no compliant way to preserve this box today.
